A1.justification: Both PDFs describe REVEAL, and their supplied text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. However, v1 cites Appendices A–D but ends after its references; v2 includes Appendices A–I. This limits comparison of earlier supplementary details, while the main-text changes remain reliably comparable.

before.justification: V1 reports original detection experiments, backbone comparisons, training ablations, and perturbation results in Tables 2–4 and Figure 5.

after.justification: V2 retains original detection results and reports additional generator evaluations, annotation ablations, human preferences, and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The stated reinforcement-learning objective changes substantially: v1 Equations 7 and 16 use advantage-weighted log probabilities with KL(old policy || current policy), whereas v2 Equations 7 and 13 use clipped probability-ratio objectives with KL(current policy || reference policy). This revises the specified optimization procedure, although implementation changes or reruns are not established. The two-stage framework and three reward components remain.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluation on REVEAL-Bench++, covering FLUX, FLUX2, Z-Image, Qwen-Image, and SD3.5 as generators stated to be absent from training. This substantially extends the evaluated generator population beyond v1's REVEAL-Bench and GenImage coverage; merely citing some generators in v1 did not establish their evaluation.

E2.justification: V2's main comparisons include AIGI-Holmes alongside retained detectors, and Table 6 adds the best individual expert, majority voting, and decision trees. AIDE and VIB-Net disappear from the full-data in-domain comparison but remain in the GenImage comparison. V2 also supplies large-model comparisons in Appendix D; v1 references such an appendix without providing its contents, so those comparisons cannot all be called newly conducted.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a balanced 10,000-image recent-generator test and an anonymized explanation study using 100 images and three annotators with majority voting. New controls test answer-first supervision and alternative annotation configurations. Section 3 also revises the reported curation sequence: v1 selects 60K images before expert annotation, whereas v2 describes selecting 60K from approximately 6M annotated samples. Newly supplied training settings do not establish changes to earlier training budgets.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained backbone, CoE/GRPO, and perturbation analyses, v2 adds an answer-first ablation, expert-guided versus direct-LLM annotation analysis, Pixel Noise expert removal, and stronger-annotator experiments. Appendices provide explanation preferences, agent-versus-embedding examples, and detailed success and failure cases. These substantially expand tests of reasoning, annotation quality, and applicability.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new three-annotator majority-vote procedure defines the human evaluation protocol; it does not introduce uncertainty estimation or inter-rater agreement statistics.

E6.justification: V2 adds recent-generator scores, answer-first accuracy of 82.39%, human preference of 63% versus 37% for AIGI-Holmes, and annotation-ablation results. Matched GenImage per-generator scores remain unchanged; the REVEAL mean changing from 95.00 to 94.96 reflects exclusion of the in-domain column. Figure 5 also revises REVEAL's robustness results under the same stated perturbations: JPEG quality 60 rises from approximately 58% to 72%, without an explanation of the revision.

T1.justification: V2 substantively revises the mathematical definitions of the GRPO and R-GRPO objectives through probability-ratio clipping and a different KL direction and reference policy. The basic GRPO advantage also gains standard-deviation normalization and a denominator safeguard. These are non-equivalent mathematical revisions, unlike the simplification of already normalized R-GRPO advantages. The SFT factorization and loss remain, and no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the expert-grounded CoE benchmark, two-stage REVEAL framework, and claims of better detection, generalization, and explanation fidelity. Although v2 moderates wording in its abstract and conclusion, its introduction retains the state-of-the-art claim and Table 1 retains the first-reasoning-dataset claim. Added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning expert aggregation, annotation reliability, complementary Pixel Noise cues, and limited gains from stronger annotation models attributed to saturation. Appendix C qualifies model-size scaling under limited data, and Appendix H acknowledges failure on a convincing synthetic cat. The multi-view reward discussion also drops v1's assertion of self-supervised discovery of novel transformation-invariant artifacts.

D1.justification: V2 supplies expert-to-input mappings, clarifies that experts operate offline without additional training, and identifies Qwen3-VL-8B as the reward assessor. It documents loss/reward weights and training details including 58K samples, 10 SFT epochs, one RL epoch, AdamW at 1e-5, and eight A800 GPUs. These are newly available disclosures, not demonstrated changes to prior settings. V2 promises future code and data release but supplies no release location.

R1.justification: The related-work framing remains largely intact. V2 adds references for DeepSeekMath, Qwen3-VL, FLUX2, Z-Image, and Qwen-Image, removes the VAR citation, and adds a limited contrast with interpretable rule-based classifiers. This updates supporting literature without substantially redefining the work's research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, and experimental narrative, expands expert and optimization explanations, incorporates backbone comparisons into the ablation section, and adds dedicated explanation and annotation sections. The author list also changes. The new template introduces unfinished running headers, including 'F. Author et al.' and 'Abbreviated paper title'.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. V1's introductory figures are replaced by a redesigned comparison diagram, while its dataset and training pipelines are retained as v2 Figures 2–3. Generalization tables are reorganized, the backbone table is transposed, and numerous analysis displays and qualitative panels are added. Figure 5 receives new styling, axes presentation, and legends alongside its separately assessed numerical revisions.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's limited support for its generalization and explainability claims through recent-generator testing, controlled annotation and reasoning analyses, and an anonymized human preference study. Supplying previously unavailable training and expert details also materially improves auditability. These gains outweigh remaining weaknesses, including unexplained Figure 5 revisions, unfinished presentation, and the new claim that alpha=0.1 prioritizes answers despite Equation 5 weighting reasoning by 0.9. The added evidence strengthens evaluation without establishing causal faithfulness.
